$description: Figure tokens of Neurodynamics-XR: the rules of every figure as machine-readable values. Read by library/styles/schematics/style.py (matplotlib), library/styles/matlab/nxr_figure_tokens.m (MATLAB) and figure_check.py; the viewer and rheome exporters are asked to read it too. The colour group is synced from the design tokens (workspace.pergammon design_tokens) by sync_colour.py; never edit it by hand. Units are in the key names (_pt, _mm). Each rule carries why it is so and its source (keys of 'sources').

elsevier-sizing.read: 2026-10-14, page text kept in the request's attachments
elsevier-sizing.says: Widths 30 / 90 / 140 / 190 mm; lettering 7 pt for normal text, no smaller than 6 pt for sub- and superscripts (rule of thumb); 300 dpi halftone, 500 dpi combination, 1000 dpi line art; consistency in size between similar diagrams.

elsevier-overview.says: Fonts Arial (or Helvetica), Courier, Symbol, Times; embed fonts.

nature-spec.cite: Nature Research figure guide: Preparing figures, our specifications.
nature-spec.says: Axis lines and tick marks; axes labelled with units in parentheses, Data (unit); accessible palette (Wong 2011); text >= 5 pt; Arial/Helvetica; avoid background gridlines, decorative icons, drop shadows, patterns, text on busy images, overlapping text, coloured text (use keylines and keys); panel letters 8 pt bold upright lower case; text 5-7 pt; scale bars on a separate editable layer, not magnification; export vector.

nature-build.cite: Nature Research figure guide: Building and exporting figure panels.
nature-build.says: Widths 89 / 183 mm; max height 170 mm to leave room for the legend; fonts 5-7 pt; panels in alphabetical order, neat, minimal white space; embed fonts (Type 42); no outlined text; avoid red/green and rainbow scales.

rougier2014.cite: Rougier NP, Droettboom M, Bourne PE (2014) Ten simple rules for better figures. PLoS Comput Biol 10(9): e1003833.
rougier2014.says: 1 know your audience; 2 identify your message; 3 adapt the figure to the support medium; 4 captions are not optional; 5 do not trust the defaults; 6 use colour effectively; 7 do not mislead the reader; 8 avoid chartjunk; 9 message trumps beauty; 10 get the right tool.

jambor2021.cite: Jambor H, Antonietti A, Alicea B, et al. (2021) Creating clear and informative image-based figures for scientific publications. PLoS Biol 19(3): e3001161.
jambor2021.says: Scale bars with dimensions on every image; insets marked at their origin; annotations and colours explained; colour-blind accessible images and labels.

crameri2020.cite: Crameri F, Shephard GE, Heron PJ (2020) The misuse of colour in science communication. Nat Commun 11: 5444.
crameri2020.says: Perceptually uniform maps; no rainbow; diverging maps for data with a meaningful centre; cyclic maps for cyclic data (phase, direction).

kovesi2015.cite: Kovesi P (2015) Good colour maps: how to design them. arXiv:1509.03700.
kovesi2015.says: Uniform perceptual contrast; cyclic maps for phase and orientation.

moreland2009.cite: Moreland K (2009) Diverging color maps for scientific visualization. ISVC 2009, LNCS 5876: 92-103.
moreland2009.says: Diverging maps: neutral centre at the reference value, ends of equal lightness.

wong2011-colour.cite: Wong B (2011) Points of view: Color blindness. Nat Methods 8: 441.
wong2011-colour.says: Colour-blind-safe palettes; do not encode by red vs green; double colour with another channel.

wong2010-gestalt.cite: Wong B (2010) Points of view: Gestalt principles (part 1). Nat Methods 7: 863.
wong2010-gestalt.says: Proximity and similarity group elements; spacing, not boxes, shows what belongs together.

wong2011-space.cite: Wong B (2011) Points of view: Negative space. Nat Methods 8: 5.
wong2011-space.says: White space separates and groups; avoid borders and dividers.

wong2011-layout.cite: Wong B (2011) Points of view: Layout. Nat Methods 8: 783.
wong2011-layout.says: Align panels to a grid; consistent alignment of axes and labels; reading order.

wong2011-arrows.cite: Wong B (2011) Points of view: Arrows. Nat Methods 8: 701.
wong2011-arrows.says: One arrow style per meaning; arrows that point at a feature are short and do not cross data.

krzywinski2013-axes.cite: Krzywinski M (2013) Points of view: Axes, ticks and grids. Nat Methods 10: 183.
krzywinski2013-axes.says: Few major ticks at round values; ticks outward; no gridlines unless values must be read; axis range to the data.

krzywinski2013-labels.cite: Krzywinski M (2013) Points of view: Labels and callouts. Nat Methods 10: 275.
krzywinski2013-labels.says: Label directly next to the data rather than in a separate legend; callouts with thin leaders; consistent placement.

krzywinski-wong2013-symbols.cite: Krzywinski M, Wong B (2013) Points of view: Plotting symbols. Nat Methods 10: 451.
krzywinski-wong2013-symbols.says: A few distinct shapes (circle, square, triangle; open vs filled); markers large enough to tell apart; overlap shown by open markers or transparency.

cleveland1984.cite: Cleveland WS, McGill R (1984) Graphical perception: theory, experimentation, and application to the development of graphical methods. J Am Stat Assoc 79: 531-554.
cleveland1984.says: Position on a common scale is read most accurately; colour (hue, saturation) least; use position for the quantity the reader must compare.

tufte.cite: Tufte ER (2001) The Visual Display of Quantitative Information, 2nd ed.; (1990) Envisioning Information. Graphics Press.
tufte.says: Data-ink; no chartjunk; small multiples share scales and layout so the eye compares content, not frames.

weissgerber2015.cite: Weissgerber TL, Milic NM, Winham SJ, Garovic VD (2015) Beyond bar and line graphs: time for a new data presentation paradigm. PLoS Biol 13(4): e1002128.
weissgerber2015.says: Show the individual data points (n small) rather than bars of means.

elsevier-neuroimage-captions.cite: NeuroImage Guide for Authors, Figure captions and Tables (Elsevier; Wayback copy 2022)
elsevier-neuroimage-captions.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
elsevier-neuroimage-captions.says: 'a brief title (not on the figure itself)'; 'Keep text in the illustrations themselves to a minimum'; no duplicated table data; no vertical rules or shading.

nature-formatting.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
nature-formatting.says: legend begins with a brief title, then each panel; no methods in legends; < 300 words; error bars and statistics defined in the legend; small tables stated in text.

nature-neuro-aip.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
nature-neuro-aip.says: panels described in sequence; centre values, error bars, n, test and P; a supplementary figure fits one page with its legend.

nature-reporting-summary.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
nature-reporting-summary.says: n as a number and unit; test and sidedness; statistic, CI, effect size, df, exact P.

plos-cb.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
plos-cb.says: a concise, descriptive caption title; table title above, notes below.

sampl.cite: Lang & Altman, SAMPL guidelines (2013; Int J Nurs Stud 2015;52:5-9)
sampl.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
sampl.says: no SE as precision, 95% CI; exact P, no 'NS', P < 0.001 floor; tables for exact values.

cobidas-meeg.cite: Pernet et al., COBIDAS MEEG (OHBM; Nat Neurosci 2020;23:1473)
cobidas-meeg.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
cobidas-meeg.says: n behind each topography; caption names the variability measure; report every effect; show unthresholded maps.

cumming2007.cite: Cumming, Fidler & Vaux 2007, J Cell Biol 177:7
cumming2007.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
cumming2007.says: describe error bars in the legend; n in the legend; plot points when n is small.

durbin2004.read: 2026-10-14 by Science (request 5356c232); quotes in its rules document and sources/
durbin2004.says: no identical information in a table and a figure; small data in a sentence.

thyng2016.cite: Thyng KM, Greene CA, Hetland RD, Zimmerle HM, DiMarco SF. True colors of oceanography. Oceanography 29(3):9-13 (2016).
thyng2016.says: Sequential for magnitudes, diverging centred on a meaningful zero for signed data, cyclic for phase. cmocean maps (MIT) are named for the quantity they serve: speed, curl, delta, diff, tempo, dense, turbid, amp.

chekhov.cite: Chekhov's gun (A. P. Chekhov, letter to A. S. Lazarev-Gruzinsky, 1 Nov 1889): every element shown must be used.
chekhov.says: Applied to figures by Diellor (2026-10-14): everything drawn is explained in a key or in the legend text.

wickham2010.cite: Wickham H (2010) A layered grammar of graphics. J Comput Graph Stat 19(1): 3-28 (ggplot2 facets).
wickham2010.says: Small multiples as a grid of facets: rows and columns by variables, shared scales, strip labels.

texbook.cite: Knuth DE (1986) The TeXbook, ch. 17-18; ISO 80000-2:2019 (mathematical signs and symbols).
texbook.says: Variables italic; operators (d, div, exp, log), constants (e, i, π) and units upright; a thin space between number and unit.

neurath.cite: Neurath O (1936) International Picture Language; ISO 7001:2023 public information symbols (pictograms).
neurath.says: A pictogram is a simplified picture of an object, readable without words at its size; detail is cut to what is legible at that size.

editor-time-sequence-2026-10-02.cite: Cortical Flow Editor design spec "Time in the Editor: the sequence and its clips" (research/code/nxr-cortical-flow/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-editor-time-sequence-and-clips-design.md), agreed by Diellor 2026-10-02
editor-time-sequence-2026-10-02.says: every tool result has tracks: its parameters along the time Line, flat when static, keyed when dynamic; masks are tracks with keyable lanes (centre, radius, level)

crane2013.cite: Crane K, Weischedel C, Wardetzky M (2013). Geodesics in heat: a new approach to computing distance based on heat flow. ACM Trans Graph 32(5):152.

type.$description: Type hierarchy at print size (pt), Pergammon theme (journal themes override). One text family; hierarchy by size and weight only, never by colour; maths by a math typesetter (type.math).

family.why: Pergammon theme: Inter, the design system's sans (app, document headings), with Greek and tabular figures. Journals that ask for Arial/Helvetica (Elsevier, Nature) set it in their theme.

embed.$value: svg: text stays text; pdf: TrueType embedded (Type 42); never outlined

colour.why: Text is never coloured; a colour is explained by a key with ink text.

figureTitle.rule: Not drawn in the artwork: the title is the first sentence of the legend (textSide.figure_title, T1). It states the finding in one declarative sentence of at most 20 words (T2), or for a figure without a finding what it shows and why (T3); never a question.
figureTitle.why: The legend is set by the journal under the figure; a title inside the artwork duplicates it and costs height.

panelLetter.place: top-left corner of the panel cell, on the cell's header line
panelLetter.why: Upper case matches the text references ('Fig. 2B'); 10 pt bold is one clear step above 8 pt headings. Nature's 8 pt bold lower case is its theme's override.

panelTitle.place: after the letter on the header line, left-aligned
panelTitle.why: One step above the 7 pt text, by weight first.
panelTitle.rule: One line in the figure, at most 60 characters, sentence case, no full stop: the panel's finding (data) or its content (schematic). No internal references (MS1 §, card or request ids), no units or n (textSide.panel_title, P1-P3).

legendText.note: the key inside the artwork; the figure legend (caption) is set by the journal

colorbarTick.why: the floor is allowed here because colourbar ticks are short numbers next to a 7 pt label; our extension of Elsevier's sub/superscript allowance

viewLabel.note: L lateral / L medial … under cortical views (the one grey text: a label of the view, not of data)

minPrint.why: Pergammon and NeuroImage: 6 pt (Elsevier: 'no smaller than 6 pt'; 5 pt printed text was a past MS1 failure). Nature's theme allows 5 pt.

math.font: Latin Modern Math: the manuscript's math font (templates/manuscripts set maths with unicode-math's default, Latin Modern Math), so a symbol in a figure looks as it does in the text
math.usetex: optional, for expressions mathtext cannot set: style.apply_figure(usetex=True) uses LaTeX (lmodern, amsmath); MATLAB: Interpreter latex
math.rule: Every symbol, Greek letter, sub- or superscript and unit exponent goes through the math typesetter ($...$ in matplotlib, Interpreter latex in MATLAB); never typed as Unicode glyphs in plain text (φ, s⁻¹, J_t).

conventions.vectors: bold as in the notation table: $\mathbf{J}$
conventions.units: upright, thin space after the number, exponents in maths: $5\,\mathrm{mm}$, $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (or m/s)
conventions.subscripts: upright when they are labels (J_\mathrm{t}, t_\mathrm{on}), italic when they are indices (x_i)

math.check: style.save warns (M1) on Greek letters or Unicode super/subscripts outside $...$

line.why: Nature's 0.25 pt is the thinnest line that prints reliably; data heavier than the frame (data-ink).

colour.$description: SYNCED from the design tokens by tokens/sync_colour.py (workspace.pergammon design_tokens). Edit the design token, not this group.

neutral-ink.meaning: Neutral: text and outlines on light backgrounds (encodes nothing)

neutral-medial-wall.meaning: Neutral: the medial wall on every cortical surface: the patch that closes each FreeSurfer hemisphere, not cortex (no grey matter). Drawn flat in this grey with a neutral-ink rim (0.5 pt) at the cortex boundary; no data colour, no colour scale, no arrows, isolines, critical points or tile fills on it (encodes nothing)

neutral-mist.meaning: Neutral light grey: empty cells, cortex shading base, fixed-atlas parcels (encodes nothing)

neutral-slate.meaning: Neutral mid-grey: rules, grid lines, secondary text, unlabelled cortex; readable on light and dark (encodes nothing)

neutral-snow.meaning: Neutral: text and outlines on dark backgrounds (encodes nothing)

trace-neutral.meaning: Neutral: a time-series trace (sensor or source signal) on light backgrounds, drawn under its detected segments (encodes nothing)

trace-neutral-dark.meaning: Neutral: a time-series trace on dark backgrounds, drawn under its detected segments (encodes nothing); dark-theme twin of trace-neutral

atlas-event.meaning: An event or dynamic scout in the dynamics atlas: the cells it occupies and its trajectory (path) through space–time cells

atlas-joint-cell.meaning: A joint space–time cell of the dynamics atlas (space node s at level ℓ × time tile k at level m)

atlas-space.meaning: Space axis of the dynamics atlas: dyadic surface tiles and space levels ℓ

atlas-time.meaning: Time axis of the dynamics atlas: dyadic time tiles and time levels m (frequency bands sit at their own time level)

flow-source.meaning: Irrotational part of a cortical vector field (Helmholtz): sources and sinks, divergence, scalar potential φ

flow-vortex.meaning: Solenoidal part of a cortical vector field (Helmholtz): vortices, curl (vorticity), stream function ψ

trace-event.meaning: A detected event on a time series: the samples of its detected segment [tOn, tOff], drawn over the neutral trace on the same line (light and dark)

atlas-coupling.meaning: Signed edge weight between two units of a connectome (e.g. α co-power, Re cross-spectrum), centred on zero: teal negative, white zero, brown positive
atlas-coupling.name: coupling: teal (negative) – brown (positive), diverging

atlas-power.meaning: Power (or power density) as a level in a cell of the dynamics atlas or the time–frequency plane, in dB re a stated reference; low dark, high bright. A contrast against a baseline takes atlas-power-contrast
atlas-power.name: power level: black – purple – yellow, sequential

atlas-power-contrast.meaning: Power contrast against a stated baseline (dB re baseline, signed): blue decrease, white no change, red increase; symmetric limits
atlas-power-contrast.name: power contrast: blue (decrease) – red (increase), diverging

atlas-tile-code.meaning: Position of a tile's code within its level (t / 2^ℓ): sibling tiles and their parent get neighbouring colours, so nesting is visible
atlas-tile-code.name: tile code: purple – green – yellow, sequential (position, not a measurement)

cortex-curvature.meaning: Curvature of the folded (pial) cortex, the anatomical base of every cortex render: pale pink on gyral crowns (curvature < 0), deep red in sulci (> 0); symmetric limits [-m, m], m = max(|p1|, |p99|). In illustrations lifted 45 % toward paper so data overlays stay readable.
cortex-curvature.name: cortex curvature: pale pink (gyri) – red (sulci), anatomy only

flow-amplitude.meaning: Amplitude (envelope) of a band-limited signal or field on the cortex, e.g. a band-limited stream-function amplitude (non-negative, from 0): low near white, high deep teal
flow-amplitude.name: band amplitude: white – teal, sequential

flow-anisotropy.meaning: Anisotropy of the tangential current orientation, (l1-l2)/(l1+l2) from 0 (isotropic) to 1 (one axis): low dark brown, high yellow
flow-anisotropy.name: anisotropy: dark brown – yellow, sequential

flow-curl.meaning: Curl (vorticity) of a cortical vector field: teal negative (clockwise seen from outside), white zero, rose positive (counter-clockwise); symmetric limits
flow-curl.name: curl: teal (clockwise) – rose (counter-clockwise), diverging

flow-divergence.meaning: Divergence div J of a cortical vector field (spreading): purple negative (sink), white zero, orange positive (source); symmetric limits
flow-divergence.name: divergence: purple (sink) – orange (source), diverging

flow-magnitude.meaning: Current magnitude |J| on the cortex (pA·m, non-negative, from 0): low dark blue-grey, high yellow
flow-magnitude.name: current magnitude: blue-grey – yellow, sequential

flow-phase.meaning: Phase or direction of a cortical quantity, cyclic from -pi to pi
flow-phase.name: phase: cyclic, black – blue – white – red – black

flow-potential.meaning: Scalar potential φ of the irrotational (Helmholtz) part of a cortical field: navy negative, white zero, olive positive; symmetric limits
flow-potential.name: potential φ: navy – olive, diverging

flow-power-share.meaning: Share of a band power, a dimensionless fraction of a whole from 0 to 1 (normal share of the source current power; relative band power): low pale yellow, high dark magenta
flow-power-share.name: power share: pale yellow – dark magenta, sequential

flow-speed.meaning: Propagation speed on the folded cortex (m/s, non-negative, from 0): low pale yellow, high dark green
flow-speed.name: speed: pale yellow – green, sequential

flow-stream.meaning: Stream function ψ of the solenoidal (Helmholtz) part of a cortical field: blue negative, pale yellow zero, green positive; symmetric limits
flow-stream.name: stream function ψ: blue – green, diverging

pet-suvr-amyloid.meaning: Amyloid-β PET uptake as SUVR (ratio to a stated reference region): low pale, high deep purple
pet-suvr-amyloid.name: amyloid SUVR: pale – purple, sequential

pet-suvr-tau.meaning: Tau PET uptake as SUVR (ratio to a stated reference region): low pale yellow, high dark brown
pet-suvr-tau.name: tau SUVR: pale yellow – brown, sequential

doc-accent.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

doc-ink.meaning: Neutral: text and headings of documents (manuscripts, slide decks) on light backgrounds (encodes nothing)
doc-ink.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

doc-muted.meaning: Neutral: secondary text of documents — subtitles, bylines, captions, minor headings (encodes nothing)
doc-muted.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

doc-unfinished.meaning: An unfinished section or placeholder in a manuscript or slide deck (press marks it): text colour of the mark
doc-unfinished.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

doc-unfinished-wash.meaning: An unfinished section or placeholder in a manuscript or slide deck: background shade behind the doc-unfinished mark
doc-unfinished-wash.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

doc-wash.meaning: Neutral: tinted background of title slides and panels in documents (encodes nothing)
doc-wash.figures: documents only (press, slides), never in data figures

nxr-cyan-50.meaning: Brand: upstream end of the neurodynamics-xr (org) mark ramp — where a streamline enters the saddle; and the node (downstream end) of the Prognome mark ramp; dark backgrounds

nxr-cyan-60.meaning: Brand: the shared cyan of the neurodynamics-xr family on light backgrounds — org ramp upstream end and Prognome node (light-theme twin of nxr-cyan-50)

nxr-green-50.meaning: Brand: downstream end of the neurodynamics-xr (org) mark ramp and upstream end (the focus) of the Rheome mark ramp; the middle dot of the 'neurodynamics·xr' wordmark; dark backgrounds

nxr-green-70.meaning: Brand: the shared green of the neurodynamics-xr family on light backgrounds — org ramp downstream end, Rheome focus, wordmark middle dot (light-theme twin of nxr-green-50)

nxr-magenta-50.meaning: Brand: the shared magenta of the neurodynamics-xr family — outer end of the Rheome mark ramp (where the spiral leaves the focus) and rim (upstream end) of the Prognome mark ramp; dark backgrounds

nxr-magenta-60.meaning: Brand: the shared magenta of the neurodynamics-xr family on light backgrounds — Rheome ramp outer end and Prognome rim (light-theme twin of nxr-magenta-50)

grid.$description: Page grid. A figure is a grid of panel cells at a journal width; every cell has a header line (letter + title) and its content below.

columns.$value: any number; cells span whole columns; letters in reading order (row-major by top-left corner)

panelPad_mm.$description: left, bottom, right, top padding inside a cell below its header: room for tick labels and axis titles so axes of neighbouring cells align

timeSeries.why: slopes near 45 degrees are read best; time runs long

sameUnitScatter.why: x and y in the same unit must share a scale or the slope misleads

cortexView.$value: native render aspect (1000 x 760 px viewer)

spectrum.$value: banked to 45 degrees: the width-to-height ratio at which the median absolute slope of the median series, on the axes drawn (log-log by default), reads at 45 degrees; a parade's cells each banked alike, never taller than wide
spectrum.why: a spectrum's 1/f slope, its peaks and departures from 1/f are read as angles, best near 45 degrees; a cell stretched tall flattens the frequency axis and exaggerates every slope

grid.keyBand_mm: legend.keyBand.row_mm per reserved row (figure(keys=...)), plus legend.keyBand.gap_below_mm

rules.rule: Axes in one row share their top and bottom edges; axes in one column share their left spine.
rules.why: the eye compares along a straight edge

rules.rule: Panel letters of a row sit on one line; headers have one height.
Panels that show the same quantity share the axis range; tick labels and axis titles only on the outer panels (small multiples).
Panels read A, B, C … left to right, top to bottom.

Views and plots in one row start at one height: the key band is reserved to the row's tallest band in every panel of the row (a panel without keys keeps the empty band), and views are anchored at the top of their cells, so a colourbar in one panel never pushes its views below the neighbours'.
rules.why: comment 23: a colourbar used in one panel only pushed its cortical view down (the crop specimen)

alignment.check: style.figure places cells on the grid; figure_check flags letters out of order

rules.rule: Draw at the final print width; never scale an export or paste a reduced crop of another figure.
rules.why: text and lines shrink below the floor (MS1 Fig. 1C printed at ~3 pt)

rules.rule: The same object keeps the same size within a figure (icons, cortical views of one kind, markers).
The smallest width that keeps every text at >= 7 pt and every mark distinguishable.

spacing.$description: Distances (mm unless _pt) at print size. White space groups and separates; no boxes.

ticks.values: round numbers; both ends of the shown range labelled when the range is not 0-based
ticks.why: outward ticks do not touch data; few round ticks are read fastest

title.rule: every axis has a title with its unit in parentheses; a time axis says ms or s; dimensionless says so ('ratio', 'z')

grid.exception: a single light reference line (0, chance, identity) in neutral-mist, 0.5 pt, dashed

range.rule: to the data, with a zero baseline wherever a quantity is a magnitude compared by length (bars)

log.rule: ticks at decades labelled 10^k or as values; say 'log scale' in the axis title only if not obvious

offset.rule: no scientific offset text ('1e-3' at the axis end): put the power in the unit, e.g. (mA/m) or (×10⁻³ s⁻¹)

omit.rule: axes are dropped only for images and cortical views, which then carry a scale bar (space) or time bar (time)

legend.$description: Keys inside the artwork (the caption is the journal's legend). REVISED (Diellor's board comment 3, 2026-10-14): one place, the key band.
legend.rule: ONE place per panel: the KEY BAND, a strip the template reserves at the top of the panel cell, under the header line (letter + heading) and above the plot area. Everything that explains a mark of the panel sits there: its colour scales (horizontal colourbars) first, then glyph keys (lines, markers, arrows, isolines, shading), left-aligned with the plot's left edge, in one row, wrapping to a second row inside the band. The band is part of the cell, so a key can never overlap the axes, their labels or a neighbouring panel.
exceptions: direct labels at the data, when ≤ 4 series and each label has free room (they replace the key entry; never over data or another label)
a key shared by several panels sits in the key band of the first panel that uses it, and the legend says "key in B applies to B–D"
never: a key over data, axis labels, ticks or a neighbouring panel
a colourbar under or beside a panel (it goes in the band)

colorbar.label: right of the bar, on its row
colorbar.ticks: under the bar, 6 pt, inside the row

keyBand.rows: 'g' = a glyph-key row (3.2 mm), 's' = a colour-scale row (5.4 mm: bar, ticks under it); figure(keys={'B': 'sg'})
keyBand.align_note: every panel whose cell starts in the same mosaic row gets the row's tallest key band (style.figure(align_keys=True), the default; nxr_figure 'AlignKeys')

legend.why: One fixed place: the reader always knows where to look, and the template can reserve the room so nothing overlaps (the v1 board's four fall-back places put keys above, inside and under panels and over labels: MS1 Fig. 1A).

placement.all: in the panel's key band (legend.keyBand): horizontal, left-aligned, its label to the right on the same row
placement.shared: one bar per quantity per figure when all panels share the scale, in the band of the first panel that uses it

colorbar.label: quantity (unit) or quantity (unit re reference)
colorbar.ticks: numbers at both ends; 0 on a diverging bar; never only '-, 0, +'
colorbar.name: the legend names the map by its descriptive name (colormapName), never by a software name (PuOr_r, cividis)

space.label: above, 7 pt, '20 mm'
space.cortex: geodesic distance on the folded surface; on inflated or sphere displays the legend says 'distances on the folded surface'
space.per: one per row of views of one size

time.label: below, 7 pt, '100 ms'
time.when: absolute time does not matter; else a time axis

amplitude.label: beside, 7 pt, with unit (pA·m, fT, µV)

scalebar.rule: editable vector bar and text, never flattened into an image; never a magnification factor

text.rule: never coloured; never over busy data without a paper halo (0.8 pt stroke)

leader.rule: straight or one elbow; does not cross data

arrow.head: filled, 2 mm
arrow.rule: one arrow style per meaning in a figure: an ink pointer points at a feature; a process arrow joins stages; a data vector is a field glyph, never a pointer

values.rule: a number in the artwork carries its unit and its uncertainty as in the text ('0.093 ± 0.01 m/s')
values.see: textSide.statistics (S1-S8): what goes in the figure, the legend and the text

inset.rule: an inset is justified only by showing MORE: a higher-resolution, more informative view of what its origin marks (a finer render, a finer mesh, a finer dyadic level), never a stretched or upsampled crop of the parent
inset.check: style.inset refuses an inset whose source has fewer than 2x the parent's pixels per mm of the object (I1)
shapes: circle: a GEODESIC DISK selection (Rheome / Editor), its outline the disk's boundary on the surface
tile: the tile's own outline (a dyadic tile selection)
inset.outline: the same shape on the origin and the inset, 0.5 pt ink; a 0.5 pt ink leader joins them when they are not adjacent
inset.multiscale: the natural inset of our framework: a whole-brain map at a coarse level with an inset of one tile at a finer level; the inset names its level ("level 7, 2 mm")
inset.selection: an inset takes the shape of the selection it shows: style.inset(..., shape='tile' | 'disk' | 'circle' | 'rect'); tile and disk insets are cut by the region's own mask, outlined by its contour
inset.revision3: REVISION 3 (Diellor's board comments 23-28, 2026-10-14; request 32d86cd6): the tile itself as an inset shape, beside square and circle; insets follow the Rheome / Editor selections

outline.$description: When a line around or between things is drawn.
outline.panel: never: cells are separated by the gutter
outline.groupSeparator: only between groups of panels that are different analyses inside one figure, and only when the gutter is not enough: one 0.5 pt neutral-mist rule across the full width
outline.image: none, except a 0.5 pt neutral-mist frame for an image with a white edge on paper
outline.inset: the same shape on origin and inset (rectangle, circle or tile outline), 0.5 pt neutral-ink
outline.glyphOnMap: every coloured arrow or patch on a colour map has an ink edge (contrast on the pink cortex, §0)

dynamics.$description: Time-varying results: which form to choose and how to lay it out.

choose.if: a scalar (or a few) changes over time
choose.use: time series (position on a common scale)

choose.if: a spatial pattern evolves and its shape matters
the pattern moves along one path
choose.use: space-time plot (distance along the path x time), with the strip optional
a supplementary video plus a strip or space-time plot in the figure

strip.interval: equal, stated once ('Δt = 20 ms') and t above each frame ('t = 40 ms')
strip.scale: one colour scale and one view for the whole strip
strip.timeAxis: thin ink time arrow under the strip

labelled.what: the event's samples drawn over the neutral trace in trace-event, 1.5× heavier, and the event named once by a direct label above its segment (≤ 3 words)
labelled.why: the cleanest look: the event is part of the signal

span.what: a shaded span (atlas-event wash, 15 % opacity, no edge) behind the traces over the event's [tOn, tOff], labelled the same way
span.when: an event defined in time rather than on one trace (several traces share it), or many short events

traceWithEvent.explain: the key band or the label names what red (or the span) is
no: a second data colour on the trace
traceWithEvent.code: style.event_trace(ax, t, x, mask, label="spindle", mode="labelled" | "span")

timeMarker.rule: one instant used elsewhere in the figure (t0 of a map) is a dashed neutral-slate rule, 0.5 pt

spaceTime.what: the joint product space of a moving pattern: time on x (ms or s), distance along the path on y (mm, geodesic on the folded surface, from the onset tile), colour = the quantity on its own map (tokens quantity)
spaceTime.reads: a travelling pattern is a straight ridge; its slope is the speed; a standing pattern is a vertical band; a reversal bends the ridge
spaceTime.guides: speed guides: dashed slate lines through the onset at stated speeds (e.g. 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 m/s), each keyed by its speed
spaceTime.grid: optionally the dyadic space-time cells as a mist grid (outlines only, never coloured: levels are the grid)
spaceTime.with: a time-track lane under it (shared x) and/or a strip; the path is drawn on a small cortex view at the left (free camera)
spaceTime.code: style.spacetime(ax, t, s, values, quantity=…, speeds=(…))

timeTrack.what: a component that shows how a parameter of a pattern changes over time: one LANE per parameter on a shared time axis (the Cortical Flow Editor tracks: a tool's parameters along the time Line, flat when static, keyed when dynamic)
parameters: position of the extremum (mm along the path, or the tile)
scale / diffusion of the heat wavelet (mm, or the level)
linked parameters (divergence, rotation and scale tied by one rule) as one lane group, the rule named

drivers.flat: constant: a flat line (a static tool)
drivers.keyed: keyframes (filled ink diamonds) joined linearly or held
drivers.analytic: a function drives the parameter: ramp (from, to), oscillation (amplitude, period, phase); named once at the lane end
drivers.measured: read from data: the detection's track

timeTrack.truthVsDetected: for analytic fields the planted track (ink line) and the detected track (atlas-event dots) share a lane: detection read against truth

layout.label: parameter (unit) left of the lane, 7 pt
layout.ticks: time tick labels on the bottom lane only
layout.playhead: a frame shown elsewhere in the figure is marked on every lane by a thin slate vertical line at its time

views.rule: both hemispheres unless the analysis has one, which the legend says; the four-view order holds in the row and the grid

surface.default: folded (pial): in figures, in panel A, in the viewer and in every exporter

options.inflated: an option for averages and whole-hemisphere overviews where sulcal data would be hidden; written "inflated" on the panel; never mixed with folded in one panel
options.sphere: geometry (tiles, gauge) and planted patterns; the radius given

surface.cropped: a cropped or zoomed view is always folded: an inflated crop is not recognisable as cortex
surface.inflated: an option, labelled, never the default

medialWall.status: DECIDED 2026-10-14 (Diellor, decision 3882c4ce: exclude; request c21de0c4; spec medial-wall-review.md §(4) layer 1)
medialWall.why: The medial wall is the patch that closes each FreeSurfer hemisphere across the corpus callosum and the diencephalic cut; it holds no grey matter. Source values there are leakage of the resolution kernel, not measurements, so nothing measured is drawn on it.
medialWall.mask: cortex = rheome.geom.select.cortex (nxr.geom.select.cortex; vertices some Desikan-Killiany (else Destrieux) parcel covers, other than unknown / corpuscallosum / Medial_wall; labels matched by prefix) or FreeSurfer ?h.cortex.label on fsaverage; wall = not cortex. A render without a mask for its surface is not a final figure.
medialWall.fill: neutral-medial-wall, flat (shading compressed to 0.85-1.0), on every view, folded, inflated and cropped
medialWall.rim: neutral-ink 0.5 pt at the cortex / wall boundary (no grey clears every diverging and cyclic centre, so the rim carries the distinction)
nothing_on_it: colour-scale limits (computed over cortex vertices only)
paths, markers and labels of results
medialWall.kept_on_it: tile outlines only where a tile itself is drawn (tiles are built on the closed surface, a geometric scaffold); anatomy-only renders (no data) may show the wall in the same grey
medialWall.exempt: the sphere and analytic surfaces (no wall); a hemisphere shown in lateral view only, where the wall is not visible (the legend phrase is still given if any medial view appears in the figure)
medialWall.legend: The medial wall (not cortex) is drawn grey, outlined; it carries no values or arrows.
medialWall.key: a grey swatch with an ink edge: "medial wall (not cortex)"

code.python (house renderer): projects/cortical-flow/draft/code/medialwall.py: wall masks (store atlas, FreeSurfer label, an exported cortex vector), paint(), rim(), keep_arrows(), limits(), LEGEND; wired into figstyle.surf_render / arrows / face_arrows (staging/ms1-figures) and brains.tiles_image
code.rheome viewer and rheome.show (the one r: asked of Methods (request c21de0c4 follow-up): read this rule and draw the wall from rheome.geom.select.cortex

arrows.rule: arrows show the FULL field by default: one arrow at every sample of the mesh the field is defined on; no striding and no random subsampling
arrows.reduce_only_if: arrows would be closer than 1 mm in print: then the field is shown at a declared coarser dyadic level (the field averaged over each tile, one arrow at each tile centre), never by dropping samples; the key says so ("arrows: J_t averaged per level-6 tile")
arrows.length: proportional to the magnitude; the key gives the scale ("arrow 2 mm = 10 pA·m")
arrows.pairing: arrows show the same vector whose magnitude or component the colour shows; otherwise each has its own key
arrows.colour: paper on dark maps, ink on light maps, with an ink edge when coloured

row.use: group averages, whole-brain events, maps compared across the cortex

grid.use: the same, compact: a narrow column or several maps side by side

free.views: any camera that shows the point (e.g. along a trajectory, a posterior-dorsal view of a spindle path); both hemispheres in view unless the point is in one
free.use: illustrations and the graphical abstract (panel A); never for a result compared across the cortex
free.label: the camera is named in the key ("view: left posterior-dorsal")

facet.what: small multiples of views: rows and columns by a variable (condition, time, band, group) × views; one colour scale; strip labels on the top row and left column only
facet.code: style.facet(F, k, rows, cols, images or draw function) — after ggplot2 facet_grid

marks.rule: Chekhov's gun on the cortex: every line, colour, marker and annotation on a cortical surface has a key entry or a legend phrase. A render declares its overlays (cortex_views(..., marks=…) or the viewer's <render>.marks.json), and E1 fails on any overlay without one.

tile outlines (shown level).key: tile outlines: level ℓ (n tiles, spacing)

selected tile or region.style: a blended fill in its axis colour (cortex.selection: atlas-space at 35 % for a space tile), outline as the other tiles

mask, scout or wavelet support.style: ink 0.8 pt dashed (2 / 1.5): an extent, never a fill
mask, scout or wavelet support.key: its name ("support of ψ at tile 13")

tile centre or atom centre.style: paper disc, ink edge, ONE size for every centre, the selected one included

path / trajectory.style: a GEODESIC on the folded surface (cortex.paths), ink 1.0 pt with an arrowhead at the end

coarser-level boundaries.style: levels.draw.multi: one weight per level, coarser heavier

selected centre.style: the same disc, filled with the selection colour
selected centre.key: "centre of tile 13" (or one entry with the selection)

marks.size: marker size never varies unless a size key gives its meaning

selection.rule: a SELECTED tile or region is a state of the surface, as in Rheome and the Editor: one colour blended inside it, never a heavy border. The selection's outline is the shown level's tile outline (0.35 pt ink), no heavier.
selection.colour: the selected cell's axis colour: atlas-space for a space tile or a geodesic disk on the cortex, atlas-time for a time tile, atlas-joint-cell for a joint cell (no new colour: the selection is a cell of that axis)
selection.centre: the selected tile's centre is the same size as every other centre, filled with the selection colour
selection.vs_support: a wavelet support or mask is an EXTENT: a dashed ink line (0.8 pt, dashes 2 / 1.5), never a fill, so a support never reads as a selection

kinds.tile: a dyadic tile (Rheome rheome.selection.wavelettile, the Editor's tile selection)
kinds.geodesic disk: all points within r mm along the folded surface (the heat-method distance); shown and inset as a circle

selection.editor_note: the Editor's mask layer desaturates the outside and edges the mask in its selection colour (--c-sel); the figure convention is the blended fill inside; Product asked to align the viewer's selection highlight (request to org:cortical-flow-lead)
selection.code: style.select_fill(ax, r.mask(v, f, in_tile), cell='space'); key: style.key(kind='patch', color=style.selection_colour('space'), alpha=0.35)

render.rule: every cortical image is rendered ONE way: the Cortical Flow viewer through rheome.snapshot (its smooth folded mesh, colours and lighting, as Diellor sees it in the viewer). No per-figure renderers (matplotlib triangles, PyVista, Brainstorm or Matlab patch screenshots), not for illustrations either.
render.marks: what is drawn ON the cortex (tile outlines, the selection, a path, centres, inset outlines) is vector, placed by the render's own camera (read from the render: the silhouette fitted, IoU >= 0.95) and hidden where the surface hides it; the scale bar is rheome.snapshot's geodesic bar
render.code: MATLAB: rheome.snapshot(surf, result, Shots=…, Out=…); Python boards: library/styles/figure-board/viewer/viewer_render.py (one MATLAB batch for the shots; ViewerRender.img / .xy / .visible / .mask); style.cortex_views records each render's provenance
render.check: V1 (figure_check, from <stem>.marks.json): a cortical image not rendered by the viewer
render.mesh: fsaverage6 (40,962 vertices a hemisphere) for whole views; fsaverage (163,842) for insets; a participant's own surface for data

paths.rule: a path on the cortex is a GEODESIC on the folded surface: traced on the mesh, never a polyline joined in the image or through the volume. Method: FlipOut (Sharp & Crane 2020, ported from geometry-central): draw.flipOut, called by nxr.geom.draw.line, rheome.geom.draw.line, the Editor's Geodesic line tool and the viewer, which draw the same line (to 1e-9 m). A FlipOut line is a geodesic, shortest among the routes near it; its length is measured along the surface and is at least the exact distance between its ends (geometry-central's MMP, exactDistance), which the viewer reports beside it (length_mm, geodesic_mm).
paths.check: G1 (figure_check, from <stem>.marks.json): a path drawn without geodesic provenance (style.path_on_cortex(..., geodesic=True, how=…))
paths.code: style.path_on_cortex(ax, F, k, r.xy(points), geodesic=True, how='FlipOut (nxr.geom.draw.line)')

icon.status: REVISION 1 (request 26698ce2, Diellor on the icon board, 2026-10-14): frames dropped; one mark at every size; no units in a mark. The icon board (library/styles/icon-board) is the rule.

icon.detail: the concept's mark with no extra detail; no text, no units, no frame, no internal hairlines, no shading; stroke 0.6-0.7 pt at 7 mm; one token colour at most
icon.use: keys, inline in diagrams, beside labels

pictogram.detail: the SAME mark as the icon, larger; it may add detail or be built from several icons at different sizes, never a different mark; neutral fills and one token colour; no units; stroke 0.5-0.8 pt
pictogram.use: panel A (graphical abstract), posters, slides, overview schematics; the current drawn set (icons.draw) is this level

illustration.detail: rendered geometry: real surfaces; fields computed (analytic or measured), never hand-drawn; cortical fields rendered by Rheome's viewer

icon.one_per_concept: one concept, ONE MARK at every size (Diellor, 2026-10-14): icon and pictogram are the same mark at different sizes; the illustration shows the same concept in rendered geometry

frames.status: DROPPED (Diellor, 2026-10-14: 'I agree. Let's drop them'); replaces decision 50f9eb81 (the framed set)
frames.was: frame shape = family (modality rounded square, field circle, operator tag, procedure hexagon; geometry, measurement, pattern none)
frames.why: at 7 mm a frame takes a third of the glyph's room; the reader does not need the family (the key names each icon); the code was arbitrary and had to be learned; three families already had no frame
frames.instead: when a figure must show family membership, the family is a word in the key, not a shape
frames.code: icons.VARIANT = 'plain' (no frame, no family mark); 'framed' / 'borderless' / 'tile' / 'twotone' only to redraw old boards

icon.rule: one mark per concept at every size; same size within a figure; colour only by token; no frames, units or text in a mark; an icon names a concept the key or legend uses, never decoration
icon.units: no units inside or under an icon or pictogram (Diellor, 2026-10-14): the unit is in the key, legend or axis (icons.draw unit=False by default)

marks.curl: a circulation around its centre point, arrow counter-clockwise (flow-vortex)
marks.trajectory: a smooth curve ending in an arrow (atlas-event); its illustration is a geodesic on the folded cortex
marks.eeg: the head from above with its nose; icon: 5 electrodes (midline + cardinal), pictogram: + the 4 diagonal

shapes.rule: at most 4 shapes in one figure; open vs filled is the second channel

marker.points: show individual values when n <= 30 (jittered strip or paired lines), with the summary over them
marker.doubleEncode: colour is never the only difference between two marks: shape or line style doubles it

phasor.status: TOKEN (revision 2, Diellor's board comment 18, 2026-10-14; designed with Methods in Rheome, request 0f976130, 2026-10-14)
phasor.meaning: phase: an angle on a circle, shown as a direction, never as a number on a line

phase.point: no amplitude: a marker on the circle (marker.size_pt, edge neutral-ink marker.edge_pt) - a distribution, the sleep study polar plot
phase.vector: with amplitude a: length a / max(a) * radius, line.arrow_pt, a filled head of min(0.22 radius, 0.6 length)

mean.length: R * radius, R = |mean(a e^{i phase})| / mean(a) (a = 1 without amplitudes)

phasor.marker: one glyph per location (at = n x 2): circle and the phase point or vector only - no ticks, no mean, no labels

implementations.python: style.phasor(ax, phase, amplitude=None, at=(0,0), radius=1, mean=None, labels=None) -> R, mu

phasor.key: the legend says the circle is |phasor| = radius, the colour is phase (flow-phase), and the dark arrow is the mean resultant

textSide.$description: Text-side rules from Science (request 5356c232, delivered 2026-10-14; Amendment 1, request 4217bca7, 2026-10-14): figure titles (T), panel headings (P), text in the figure vs the legend (X), legend structure (L), colour-map naming (C6), Chekhov's gun (E1, E2), statistics (S), tables vs figures (B). Each rule id is defined and cited in the board §21 and in Science's rules document (figure-text-rules.md, with request 5356c232). Read by style.figure and nxr_figure (panel_title.max_chars), figure_check.py (P1, P3, E1 from <stem>.marks.json) and legend_check.py (T, L, S, C6, E2).
textSide.owner: org:study-manager (rules); org:design-lead (implementation in the code and the board)

figure_title.form: the finding stated so that a reader of the introduction understands it AND it is exact: name the measured thing, the comparison or condition and the result, in the words the introduction uses for the gap or question; it may take more than one sentence (theme limit). A figure without a finding (schematic, data, method) states what it shows and why (T3).
forbidden: bare topic noun phrase when the figure tests something
claims stronger than the statistics in the same legend

plain_and_precise.plain: no in-group shorthand ("operator", "plant", "exact") without saying what it is; a reader of the abstract can follow it
plain_and_precise.precise: names the quantity, the condition and the result; never stronger than the statistics; a null stated as a null

tie.what: every title states (part of) a claim or hypothesis of the paper; the figure card records it in `supports:` (claim or hypothesis id); the id is never printed

figure_title.limits_are: theme values: the Pergammon theme keeps the longer limits, journal themes cut them (theme.*.overrides)

examples.before: Every operator is exact where truth is known.
examples.after: On a sphere, where the true answer is known in closed form, each measurement (size, direction, speed, path, divergence and rotation) returns the planted value; panels F-L show how far each drifts with noise.
examples.commentary: A measure is only trusted if it returns a known answer; this separates errors of the measurement from those of the instrument, which Fig. 9 tests.

examples.before: Which reported patterns survive the instrument.
examples.after: Large reported cortical waves (80–200 mm wavelength) keep their speed, wavelength, rotation and chirality when measured through MEG; smaller patterns (16–57 mm) do not.
examples.note: ranges from the MS1 Fig. 9 legend; Science checks the wording against Results 2.7.2
examples.commentary: Whether a reported wave can be measured at all depends on its scale relative to what MEG resolves.

panel_title.form: a short heading: the panel's finding (data panels) or its content (schematic panels), sentence case, no full stop
panel_title.letter_in_legend: bold upper-case letter followed by what is plotted
forbidden_in_heading: internal references (MS1 §, MS1 Table, card or request ids)
units or n (they go on axes and in the legend)

allowed: keys (in the key band, legend.keyBand) and direct labels
colourbar titles with quantity and unit
short annotations naming a marked feature (<= 8 words)
n per group when the panel compares groups
panel-A step labels (<= 4 words each, noun phrases)
legend_material: full sentences explaining how to read the panel
statistics beyond n and the marked values
cross-references to other figures, tables or sections

panel_A_text_strip.status: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-14 (Diellor's board comment 2; Science Amendment 1, X4): replaced by panelA

panel_A.form: a mini graphical abstract (tokens panelA): data -> condition -> approach on example data -> detected, left to right; a step that carries nothing is left out
panel_A.label_form: a noun phrase that names ("EEG, 64 channels", "N2 sleep", "spindle path, m/s"); never a sentence or an explanation
panel_A.marks: every drawn mark (icon, highlighted event, arrow) explained in the key band or in legend entry A (E1)
panel_A.legend_entry_A: the description in one or two sentences: dataset and n with its unit; the example (participant, duration, channel or hemisphere); the event and the measure; procedures go to Methods (L4)

keys.where: the panel's key band (legend.keyBand); direct labels replace a key entry for <= 4 series with room
keys.key_vs_legend: the key gives the short name of a mark; the legend entry says what it means when the name alone does not (quantity, unit, isoline step); it does not repeat the key word for word

in_figure_text.X1: No sentences in figures, as a general rule: the sentences go in the legend. An exception must be informative (e.g. a definition the reader needs at the mark) and is declared in code (style.allow_sentence(reason)); style.save and figure_check report every other sentence (X1).

legend.panel_entry: **X** what is plotted: quantity (unit); what each mark, line, colour and shading is; the n behind it; centre and spread (named); the test if a p is shown; colour maps by descriptive name (C6); every mark not explained in the key band (E1)
legend.methods_in_legend: pointer only ("Section 4.x"); parameters needed to read the panel may be named, procedures are not described
forbidden: repo@commit, script names, request or card ids, bracketed editorial notes
error bars or shading without saying what they are
n missing for any panel with a group statistic
a term not in the manuscript's notation table or used with a different name in the figure

commentary.where: right after the title, before panel entry A
commentary.what: why the figure is shown: the idea it communicates and the question or gap of the introduction it answers (e.g. "A measure is only trusted if it returns a known answer; this separates errors of the measurement from those of the instrument, which Fig. 9 tests."). No new results, no methods.

legend.description_then_why: the panel entries describe what we see; the commentary says why we show it
legend.limits_are: theme values: Pergammon (house) keeps the longer limits; journal themes cut them

colormap_naming.rule: a colour map is named by what it encodes, never by its software name
colormap_naming.in_legend: quantity (unit) and the colours at the ends with their meaning, e.g. 'colour: divergence (s⁻¹), purple sinks to orange sources, centred on 0'; a diverging map states its centre; every scale states whether it is clipped
colormap_naming.in_key: the colourbar carries quantity, unit and ticks
forbidden: software or package map names in keys and legends (PuOr_r, RdBu_r, viridis, cividis, magma, cmo.*, jet)
colormap_naming.software_names_go: Methods, once, citing the published map collection used (e.g. cmocean); never in a legend (L6)
colormap_naming.check: legend_check.py C6; a bare cmocean name without 'cmo.' (curl, speed, phase) is also a quantity name and is not flagged: a human checks

explain.rule: Chekhov's gun: every class of mark in a panel is explained in the key band or in the panel's legend entry; nothing is explained that is not shown (L3)
explain.explained_means: the reader can say what the mark represents (quantity, event, reference) without Methods; naming its style ('dashed line') is not enough
explain.self_labelling: scale and time bars with their value, direct labels, annotations, axis titles

which_place.key_band: what the eye needs while reading the panel: colours, line and marker styles, arrows
which_place.legend: what a mark means or how it was obtained: a contour's level, what a shaded span contains

explain.unexplainable: a mark that cannot be explained in a short key entry or a legend clause is removed or given its own panel
explain.E2: a mark recorded as style.explain(..., where='legend') has its recorded phrase, word for word, in that figure's legend

in_figure: individual participants as points when n <= 30 per group (else distribution: violin/box with points or density)
the reference line of the null or chance
significance marks only if defined in the legend (prefer exact values in text)
n per group label when groups are compared
in_legend: n per group and the unit of n (participants, hemispheres, plants, recordings)
centre (median/mean) and the interval named (95% CI percentile bootstrap, IQR, SD …)
the test, sidedness, paired or independent, multiplicity correction (name only)
what any threshold, contour or shading means
in_text: test statistic and df where defined

p_format.style: p = 0.03; two significant digits; p < 0.001 below 0.001
never: p < 0.05 when the exact value is available

statistics.ci_and_test_must_agree: if a CI computed without multiplicity adjustment is shown beside an adjusted p, say so in Statistics (Section 4.10) once
statistics.thresholded_maps: show the unthresholded map as well (main or supplementary) and name the threshold

use_table_when: the reader needs exact values to compare or re-use
many quantities per unit with few units (e.g. <= ~10 rows × <= ~8 columns)
definitions, notation, parameters, participant counts, rules of use
use_figure_when: the message is a pattern, trend, distribution or comparison
values per participant or per vertex
tables_vs_figures.never_duplicate: the same numbers in a table and a figure; keep the table in the supplement if both are needed

theme.$description: Themes (Diellor's board comment 1, 2026-10-14): a journal's requirements are never the default values. The base token groups are the Pergammon theme, ours; a journal theme overrides only what that journal requires (dotted paths into the token groups) and sets its page. Add a journal by adding a theme; nothing else changes. A manuscript picks its theme from its manuscript template (templates/manuscripts/<journal>).

pergammon.name: Pergammon (house)
pergammon.why: Our own look: the design system's sans (Inter, as in the Pergammon app and our documents) and a page that fits every journal theme in the library at 1:1 (88 / 136 / 180 mm, ≤ 170 mm tall fit both NeuroImage and Nature), so a default figure never has to be rescaled.

neuroimage.name: NeuroImage (Elsevier)
neuroimage.note: max height 240 mm is the printed text area minus room for the legend: our rule, to confirm at proof (Elsevier gives no figure height).
neuroimage.text_limits_note: [our choice] where the journal states no number: Elsevier asks for "a brief title" and minimal text; Nature for a brief title and legends of about 300 words (rev. 1 L5). Re-check at submission.

nature.name: Nature journals
nature.note: onehalf 136 mm is not in the fetched guide text; used only for checks. Nature gives two width pairs: 89/183 mm (figure guide, used here) and 90/180 mm (formatting guide); a figure at 89/183 fits both within 1 mm (researcher's shelf, 2026-10-14).
nature.text_limits_note: [our choice] where the journal states no number: Elsevier asks for "a brief title" and minimal text; Nature for a brief title and legends of about 300 words (rev. 1 L5). Re-check at submission.

theme.$note_overrides_list: overrides_list repeats overrides as {path, value} pairs for MATLAB (jsondecode cannot keep dotted keys); edit overrides and re-run the generator line in tokens/README or keep both equal.

panelA.status: REVISED (Diellor's board comment 2, 2026-10-14): replaces the ≤ 30-word text strip (open point 5, Science X4)
panelA.role: The figure's topic sentence, drawn: a mini graphical abstract of the study behind the figure. The figure groups its results under one idea, stated like a study statement (e.g. 'Prefrontal amyloid-β predicts cognitive deficits'); that statement is the figure title (textSide T2) and panel A shows how it was studied.

steps.shows: the data collection: the modality (EEG cap, MEG helmet, PET scanner …) and who or what was recorded
the condition or question (sleep, rest, a task, a group contrast)
steps.form: pictogram or a strip of example data (a hypnogram, a task timeline) + label

steps.shows: the analysis illustrated on example data: e.g. cortical flow on one example recording
steps.form: example data with the detection drawn on it (events on the trace, a field on the cortex)

steps.shows: what is detected or measured: the event or pattern, named, and the measure with its unit
steps.form: example (a pattern on the cortex, free camera) + label with the unit

panelA.order: left to right in reading order, joined by process arrows (annotation.arrow: process); a step may be omitted when it carries nothing (e.g. no condition)

text.description: legend entry A says it in words

panelA.span: the full figure width, first row
panelA.uses: pictograms and illustrations from the media library and example data of this study: composed, never redrawn; every mark explained (explain)
panelA.example: EEG cap (data) → sleep, N2 on a hypnogram (condition) → EEG with one spindle labelled (approach on example data) → the spindle's path on the cortex, speed (m/s) (detected)

layout.rule: Every artist of a panel stays inside its cell (header, key band and plot area); nothing overlaps an artist of another panel; inside a panel no text overlaps other text or a key.

controls.pads: padding per kind or per panel (grid.panelPad_mm; figure(pads=...))
controls.text: annotate() and direct_label() are checked like every other artist
controls.fix: more room (widths, heights, pads), fewer or shorter words, or a key entry instead of a direct label

layout.check: style.check_layout(F) runs in style.save (raises on an overlap unless save(..., layout="warn")); figure_check O1 (text boxes overlapping) on PDF and SVG

codes.O2: an artist leaves its panel cell
codes.O3: a key or colourbar overlaps axes, ticks or labels
codes.O4: an axes element (tick labels, axis title, offset text, axes text) enters its panel header or key band
codes.O5: panels of one row whose key bands end, or whose views start, at different heights
codes.O6: panels of a stack with different x ranges or plot edges

layout.revision2: REVISION 2 (Diellor's board comment 17, 2026-10-14; request 5539a667): O4 added; the plot pad top is 2 mm so the top tick label clears the heading; offset text is checked like other text

stack.rule: Panels that share an x axis (time, frequency) may be STACKED on one base: one x axis at the bottom, the plots' left and right edges aligned, the x range shared, no x tick labels or title above the bottom part; the parts sit gap_mm apart instead of a gutter and a header. Each part keeps its letter (top left, beside its plot) and its y label; a lower part has no heading (it goes in the legend); the stack's keys go in the key band of its top panel.
stack.when: a space-time plot and its time-tracks; a trace, its spectrogram and its event raster; band power and phase over frequency: whenever the reader compares the parts at the same x
stack.code: style.stack(F, ['B', 'C']) right after style.figure(...); MATLAB nxr_stack(F, 'BC')
stack.check: O6: the stack's x ranges and plot edges

explain.rule: Everything shown is explained. Every class of mark in a panel (trace, line, marker, arrow or vector glyph, isoline, shading or span, colour map, critical point, outline, reference line, region) is named either in the panel's key band or in the panel's legend entry. Self-labelling marks explain themselves: scale and time bars with their value, direct labels, annotations, axis titles.
examples: a scalar map with coloured arrows: the colourbar explains the colour AND a key entry (or the legend) says what the arrows are
a colour map with isolines: the colourbar AND a key entry 'isolines: every 0.2 s⁻¹'
a grey disc on the cortex: 'start region' in the key
explain.code: style tracks the marks of every panel; style.explain(artist, text, where="key"|"legend"); style.save writes <stem>.marks.json and warns on unexplained marks (E1); legend_check --marks checks the legend-explained ones against the legend entry

illustration.$description: The ILLUSTRATION look: one camera-attached light rig, one material, one silhouette rule and role colours, shared by the PyVista recipe (library/styles/illustrations/recipe.py reads this group) and the Cortical Flow viewer's look 'illustration' (nxr-cortical-flow editor/src/viewer). No number of the look is written in either renderer. Objects encode nothing: roles map to neutrals only. Shape: the viewer's IllustrationTokens (nxr-cortical-flow editor/src/viewer/illustration.ts): lights [{name, dir, intensity}], material {ambient, diffuse, specular, power}, silhouette {colour, width_pt, atWidth_mm}, role {role: colour token}, cortex {colormap, mute, muteTo, tone}; the other keys are the recipe's and are ignored by the viewer.
illustration.status: DRAFT 2026-10-14 (Graphics, request cc624568; design edbf0aca part 2): the values are the recipe's as rendered since 2026-10-08, moved here unchanged; acceptance is the side-by-side review of cf-ill-eeg (PyVista vs viewer) after the viewer's look PR

lights.name: key
lights.why: upper left, in front: the reading light

lights.name: fill
lights.why: right, low: opens the shadow side

lights.name: rim
lights.why: behind, above: separates the silhouette from the background

illustration.$lights: Camera-attached directional lights. dir: the direction from the scene TOWARD the light in the CAMERA basis (+x screen right, +y screen up, +z toward the viewer), not normalised (normalise before use). intensity: VTK's light intensity (the viewer scales to its own light model so the side-by-side matches; the ratios key:fill:rim are the rule).

material.$description: One Phong material for every mesh (VTK lighting coefficients). The ambient term is ambient x the object's own colour (no separate ambient light). smooth: per-vertex normals interpolated.
material.overrides: an object may raise its specular (glossy device shells: 0.35-0.45), stated in its object.json 'material'; nothing else changes per object

silhouette.$description: An ink outline on the outer silhouette of every mesh (creases inside a mesh are not drawn), unlit.

reference.why: the recipe's 6 px at a 1600 px render is 0.2657 pt when the illustration prints atWidth_mm (25 mm) wide (illustrations print 15-30 mm); width_pt at atWidth_mm is the rule, px derive from it at the actual render size

weights.$description: silhouette width as a fraction of width_pt, by object (object.json 'silhouette'): the recipe's sil_w 2.5 / 2.0 / 1.5 -> default / secondary / fine; rims: the scanners' rims (feature edges) at 0.6; none: no outline (bore linings, detector blocks)

silhouette.why: one line weight across the illustration set so a scalp, a dewar and a brain drawn apart still look drawn by one hand

$role.$description: Scene-object role -> neutral colour token (a key of colour.neutral). An object's object.json 'color' (a neutral name or #rrggbb) overrides its role.

meaning.device2: bores, detector rings, tables, caps, toolboxes

background.why: illustrations are placed on the figure page; the render is cropped to its content plus a 12 px pad

cortex.$description: The cortex in an illustration: cmocean amp (colormaps/amp.json; token cortex-curvature) of the folded (pial) surface's mean curvature, FreeSurfer sign (sulci > 0), lifted toward paper by mute. Without a curvature field, one flat tone. tone: the viewer's flat cortex when a bundle carries no curvature (a colour token); tone_index/tone_hex: the recipe's flat tone for parametric cortex (sheets, glass): amp[tone_index] lifted by mute (not a colour token; it encodes nothing)
cortex.range: symmetric [-m, m], m = max(|p1|, |p99|) (the viewer's autoRange)
cortex.why: the cortex reads as tissue (pink, biological) without competing with any data colour laid over it

objects.$description: The recipe's geometry, exported once (positions.bin float32 [n x 3], faces.bin int32 [m x 3] 0-based, object.json): library/media/illustrations/objects/<name>/, built by library/styles/illustrations/export_objects.py

colormapName.$description: Descriptive names of the colormap tokens (Diellor's board comment 6, 2026-10-14): what the map encodes, its colours low to high, its type. Used in UIs (viewer, Pergammon), keys and legends instead of software names (PuOr_r). Merged into colour.colormap.<token>.name by sync_colour.py.
colormapName.flow-stream: stream function ψ: blue – green, diverging
colormapName.atlas-power: power level: black – purple – yellow, sequential
colormapName.pet-suvr-tau: tau SUVR: pale yellow – brown, sequential
colormapName.atlas-tile-code: tile code: purple – green – yellow, sequential (position, not a measurement)
colormapName.flow-phase: phase: cyclic, black – blue – white – red – black
colormapName.cortex-curvature: cortex curvature: pale pink (gyri) – red (sulci), anatomy only
colormapName.flow-power-share: power share: pale yellow – dark magenta, sequential

quantity.$description: ONE COLORMAP PER QUANTITY (Diellor's board comment 7, 2026-10-14): different quantities get different maps even when both are sequential (current magnitude vs PET SUVR) or both diverging (divergence vs curl). Within a scale type the maps differ in at least one end hue. A quantity not listed gets its map from Graphics (a new token) before it is plotted. Keys are what style.colorbar(kind=...) and nxr_colorbar take.

suvr_amyloid.unit: SUVR (ratio re a stated reference region)
suvr_amyloid.limits: a level; the threshold, if any, named

suvr_tau.unit: SUVR (ratio re a stated reference region)

aliases.signed: divergence (retired kind: say which signed quantity)

never: hsv (except as a cyclic map by token)
one map for two quantities in a figure
a software name (PuOr_r) in a legend or UI

levels.rule: dyadic levels are the grid, not a field: the increments of the parcellation of space and time over the manifold, like the grid spacing of Euclidean space and the spacing used for the calculations and the differential operators. A level never gets a colormap and a tile is never coloured by its level or code in a data figure.

draw.space: tile outlines in ink, the levels shown by weight (levels.draw.multi: up to three, 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 pt, coarser heavier); one level alone at 0.35 pt; a tile is named by its number, never a colour
draw.time: tile boundaries as lines on the time axis by the same weights, in slate (style.level_lines)
draw.spacing: a level is stated by its spacing: "level 4 (16 tiles, about 33 mm)"

multi.rule: several levels at once are drawn like the major and minor grid lines of a 2-D plot: one line weight per level, coarser levels heavier, each boundary drawn once at its coarsest level (coarser boundaries are a subset of finer ones), as isolines show several values
multi.key: one entry per level, by weight: "level 3: 8 tiles, 50 mm"
multi.code: cortex: style.level_weights(n) for the tile outlines; plots: style.level_lines(ax, (t0, t1), [2, 3, 4])
multi.plot_note: on a plot the lines are grid lines: mist, behind the data, so they never compete with a trace

slice.what: one cortical depth (a spatial level) is a slice through the dyadic stack of space tiles
slice.indicator: the level indicator: a z-stack glyph of the depths as stacked bars of halving width, FINER UP (depth 0, the coarsest, at the bottom), the shown depth filled ink, the others mist outlines; labelled by what it measures, "depth 4 · ≈ 90 mm" (equivalent-disc diameter from the tile table of the cortex shown, never a formula, never an index alone); when a MEG reading is shown, a dashed slate rule marks the MEG separation floor (2 r50 ≈ 95–100 mm) and the finer depths beyond it are drawn lighter
slice.code: style.level_indicator(ax, n_levels, shown, spacing_mm={depth: mm}, floor=dict(depth=3, text='MEG floor ≈ 95–100 mm'))
slice.status: REVISION 4 2026-10-14 (Science's level-stack review, request ef2c73a0): finer up, spacing printed, MEG floor

volume.status: REVISION 4 2026-10-14 (Science's level-stack review, request ef2c73a0): split into two modes; not for MS1 figures until the depth/level term and the alpha tile duration (164.8 ms vs 8–16 Hz) are settled
volume.rule: two time volumes that must not be mixed; both finer up; neither has a spatial axis (a time tile is linked to no cortical depth)

scalogram.what: time x octave (the Heisenberg tiling): one row per octave band, its tiles the band's time tiles of the duration the tile table gives (one cycle of the band's lowest frequency), so a row holds duration x f_low tiles; rows labelled "8–16 Hz · 125 ms" (band, tile duration); a value per tile on its quantity's map, or outlines only
scalogram.rollup_outline: never: tiles of different bands do not sum each other
scalogram.code: style.level_scalogram(ax, (t0, t1), bands=[dict(f_low=, f_high=, tile_s=), …], values=None)

pyramid.what: time x aggregation level within ONE band: the parent tile at the bottom, each row up halving the tiles, the band's own time tiles at the top; rows labelled by tile duration ("0.66 s"), the band named in the key; the field is the sums of the band's LINEAR power (exact roll-up); if shown in dB the legend says the sums are of linear power
pyramid.rollup_outline: yes: a tile and the tiles it rolls up into (cell=)
pyramid.code: style.level_pyramid(ax, t0, tile_s, n_levels, power=linear, band='alpha 8–16 Hz', db=True)

volume.index: figures name a level by what it measures (space: depth d, coarse = 0, with its equivalent-disc mm; time: band and tile duration); the atlas store's finest = 0 index stays in Rheome and is converted in one Rheome function, never in figure code

levels.tile_code_map: atlas-tile-code is not used for levels or tiles in data figures; it stays only for the dyadic-code schematic (S6) until Science and Methods review the level visualisation
